transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Linda Kenyon.
Invidia stocks opened down this morning, reversing some of yesterday's gain after CEO Jensen
Huang was reinstated.
Ricky Mulvey with NPR's The Indicator from Planet Money addresses why investors were
so happy about Huang's return.
Jensen Huang is Invidia.
Researchers were happy to put the scandals aside and said that Jensen Huang is a good
chunk of the company's value.
And that boost, about $950 billion of market cap, is the biggest one-day gain for a single
company ever.
And for context, that's in the ballpark of all of Walmart's stock, who, as you
may know, is the largest private sector employer in the United States.
Huang had resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including with a woman suspected
of spying for China.
President Trump says he personally intervened to have him reinstated.
Democratic Congressman Jimmy Gomez of California is resigning.
NPR's Sam Gringlass says the announcement follows a bipartisan investigation that found
substantial evidence Gomez engaged in sexual misconduct toward a staff member.
The House Ethics Committee concluded his actions violated House rules by "making unwelcome
sexual advances and engaging in unwelcome sexual conduct toward a House staffer."
The report also found the behavior could constitute criminal sexual assault.
Gomez lost reelection this fall and denied the encounters were nonconsensual.
In a statement, he wrote he had strong disagreements with the report and its conclusions.
The committee said Gomez's actions point to a broader culture of disrespect and toxic
sexual behavior toward staff that permeates life on the Hill and is long overdue for correction.
This year, two other House members have also resigned amid sexual misconduct allegations.
And last week, the Ethics Committee unveiled new rules to help speed investigations and
improve transparency.
Sam Gringlass, NPR News, Washington.
Acting Army Secretary Adam Tell says a controlled detonation of hazardous material at an Iowa
Army ammunition plant will go forward tomorrow, now that an appeals court has approved the
plan.
At a briefing with federal officials, Tell explained why the controlled detonation is necessary.
There is consensus across the experts, across the country, that a controlled, mitigated
detonation of the lead azide here at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is far preferable to
an uncontrolled, spontaneous detonation of that substance.
Some residents and environmental experts say they are concerned about the amount of lead
particles that could float into the atmosphere and with wind gusts that could travel roughly
100 miles away.
Officials say the planned detonation is scheduled for tomorrow morning.
You're listening to NPR.
A group of prominent writers is banding together to form a new free speech group called Penn
Rights USA, NPR's Andrew Limbong has the story.
Ta-Nehisi Coates, Percival Everett, and Em Gessen are just a few of the big name writers
who are members of Penn Rights USA.
The group is working with a broader free speech group Penn International to be recognized
as an official chapter.
Founding member Francine Prose says in a statement that writers have a unique role in promoting
free speech, not just by writing, but "in deciding what an organization like ours stands
for."
This is a former president of PEN America, which has gone through a lot of upheaval lately,
particularly over its responses to free speech debates over the war in Gaza.
That org sent a statement to NPR saying it remains committed to protecting free expression
regardless of viewpoints.
Andrew Limbong, NPR News.
It's an event fans have been anticipating for years.
The Irish rock band U2 has announced a North American leg of its worldwide tour following
the release of the group's first album in nine years.
The album is called "Carnival De Luz."
The tour is titled "Carnival De Luz Presents the Greatest Show on Earth World Tour, 2027."
The band plans on mixing its classic hits with new songs, while the album concludes
with a collaboration with Dolly Parton.
This marks her last vocal recording before her death in August at the age of 80.
The North American tour will kick off in Miami on August 13th and will wrap up in Vancouver
on October 18th.
Pre-sale of tickets will begin Monday.
I'm Lynda Kenyon, NPR News in Washington.

topics.text: Invidia stock opens down after CEO Jensen Huang's reinstatement, reversing yesterday's gain
Jensen Huang's return adds roughly $950 billion to Nvidia's market cap, largest one-day gain ever
Democratic Congressman Jimmy Gomez of California resigns after House Ethics Committee finds sexual misconduct
Acting Army Secretary Adam Tell says Iowa Army Ammunition Plant detonation will proceed after appeals court approval
Prominent writers including Ta-Nehisi Coates form Penn Rights USA free speech group
U2 announces North American leg of 2027 tour following first album in nine years
